split_reasoning: Managing backup, security, and user help systems involves different operational services and produces different management outputs.

parts.text: Manage the operation of backup systems, including addressing backup exceptions.
parts.type_reasoning: A backup exception can be investigated and resolved as a distinct operational item.
parts.unit_reasoning: An exception is tracked through resolution and relied on by the operations team.
parts.work_item: one backup exception investigated and addressed
parts.start: backup failure or other exception is reported
parts.end: corrective action is recorded or assigned and the exception is resolved or escalated
parts.checked_by: IT operations staff and the systems manager
parts.overlap_reasoning: Developing recovery resources is related but broader than managing an operational backup exception.

parts.text: Manage security systems, including addressing security exceptions.
parts.type_reasoning: A security exception produces a distinct investigation and disposition.
parts.unit_reasoning: The exception is handled as a case rather than as an individual monitoring action.
parts.work_item: one security exception investigated and addressed
parts.start: security alert or exception is reported
parts.end: disposition and any corrective action are recorded or escalated
parts.checked_by: security staff and the systems manager
parts.overlap_reasoning: Security resource development is related but is not the same as managing an operational exception.

parts.text: Manage user help operations, including resolving escalated help-service issues.
parts.type_reasoning: An escalated service issue has a distinct disposition relied on by help staff.
parts.unit_reasoning: The escalated issue is the operational case handed to the manager.
parts.work_item: one escalated user-help issue addressed
parts.start: help-service issue or escalation is received
parts.end: resolution or further escalation is communicated to help staff
parts.checked_by: help desk staff and the affected user
parts.overlap_reasoning: Escalated user problems can involve technical support, while each statement also covers other work.

notes: The shares and mix of operational exceptions depend on how much direct oversight the manager delegates.

split_reasoning: Consulting different stakeholders serves the same activity of assessing computing needs and requirements.

parts.text: Consult users, management, vendors, and technicians about computing needs and system requirements.
parts.type_reasoning: The target describes consultation, whose value lies in the live exchange of information.
parts.overlap_reasoning: These consultations can inform technology evaluations and project feasibility reviews, but those statements also cover separate evaluations.

notes: A separately prepared requirements document is not specified by the target.

split_reasoning: Directing daily staff operations, setting operational priorities and deadlines, and developing standards are different activities.

parts.text: Direct staff on daily departmental operations.
parts.type_reasoning: Day-to-day direction is primarily live supervision and coordination.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Daily direction can include supervision and work assignments, but those statements also cover other staffing and review work.

parts.text: Analyze departmental workflow and set operational priorities and deadlines.
parts.type_reasoning: The analysis produces an operational work plan that staff use to organize their work.
parts.unit_reasoning: A plan for a work period is a usable handoff to the department.
parts.work_item: one departmental operational work plan
parts.start: current workload, deadlines, and staff capacity are reviewed
parts.end: priorities and deadlines are set and communicated to staff
parts.checked_by: department staff and management
parts.overlap_reasoning: Operational planning can inform project coordination and individual assignments, which have their own outputs.

parts.text: Develop standards for departmental operations.
parts.type_reasoning: A documented operational standard is a distinct output staff can apply.
parts.unit_reasoning: A standard is issued and used as a whole.
parts.work_item: one departmental operating standard
parts.start: need for a new or revised standard is identified
parts.end: standard is finalized and communicated to staff
parts.checked_by: department staff and management
parts.overlap_reasoning: Operating standards can take the form of organizational procedures, although the other statement also covers goals and interpretation.

notes: Shares vary with the department's management structure.

split_reasoning: Assigning work and reviewing completed work are distinct activities with different outputs.

parts.text: Assign work to systems analysts, programmers, and other computer-related staff.
parts.type_reasoning: An assignment gives a staff member a defined piece of work to carry out.
parts.unit_reasoning: An individual work assignment is the handoff to the assigned worker.
parts.work_item: one staff work assignment
parts.start: work needing assignment and staff availability are identified
parts.end: assignment and expectations are communicated to the worker
parts.checked_by: the assigned worker and the manager
parts.overlap_reasoning: Assignments are part of daily direction and supervision, but the other statements cover broader management activities.

parts.text: Review work completed by systems analysts, programmers, and other computer-related staff.
parts.type_reasoning: Each review produces feedback or an acceptance decision on a submitted work product.
parts.unit_reasoning: The submitted work product is reviewed and returned or accepted as a whole.
parts.work_item: one staff work product reviewed
parts.start: staff member submits work for review
parts.end: feedback or acceptance is communicated to the worker
parts.checked_by: the staff member and downstream users of the work
parts.overlap_reasoning: Reviewing systems charts and programs is a subset of reviewing staff work, while each statement also covers other review items.

notes: Assignments may be communicated verbally or through a work-tracking system.

split_reasoning: Staying current with technology is one continuing activity.

parts.text: Keep current with advances in technology.
parts.type_reasoning: The target describes maintaining knowledge rather than producing a specified output for others.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Technology knowledge may inform evaluations, but the target does not itself describe an evaluation deliverable.

split_reasoning: Strategic computing, security controls, and disaster recovery call for different resource plans or arrangements.

parts.text: Develop strategic computing resources and plans for the organization.
parts.type_reasoning: A strategic computing plan is a distinct output used for resource decisions.
parts.unit_reasoning: The plan is reviewed and used as a whole.
parts.work_item: one strategic computing resource plan
parts.start: organizational computing needs and objectives are identified
parts.end: resource plan is documented and submitted for review
parts.checked_by: management and IT leadership
parts.overlap_reasoning: Technology evaluations and recommendations can feed the resource plan, but are not necessarily the same deliverable.

parts.text: Develop data security and control arrangements for information resources.
parts.type_reasoning: A security and control design is a distinct output for implementation.
parts.unit_reasoning: The control arrangement for a defined system or scope is handed to implementers as a whole.
parts.work_item: one data security and control design
parts.start: system scope, security needs, and control requirements are identified
parts.end: control design is documented and handed to the responsible team
parts.checked_by: security staff, system owners, and management
parts.overlap_reasoning: Managing security systems concerns ongoing operations, whereas this part develops control arrangements.

parts.text: Develop disaster recovery arrangements for information resources.
parts.type_reasoning: A disaster recovery plan is a distinct output used by recovery teams.
parts.unit_reasoning: The plan for a defined recovery scope is reviewed and maintained as a whole.
parts.work_item: one disaster recovery plan
parts.start: recovery scope and requirements are identified
parts.end: plan is documented and submitted to responsible teams
parts.checked_by: IT operations, management, and recovery personnel
parts.overlap_reasoning: Backup-system management supports recovery but also covers operational work outside plan development.

notes: Actual resource development may include additional implementation work depending on the organization.

split_reasoning: Reviewing charts and programs is the same approval activity applied to different submitted system artifacts.

parts.text: Review and approve systems charts or programs before implementation.
parts.type_reasoning: Each submitted artifact receives a review and an approval or revision decision.
parts.unit_reasoning: The submitted chart or program is the item accepted or returned for changes.
parts.work_item: one systems chart or program reviewed for implementation
parts.start: chart or program is submitted for approval
parts.end: approval or required revisions are communicated
parts.checked_by: the submitting staff member and implementation team
parts.overlap_reasoning: This is a particular kind of staff work review, while the broader review statement covers other work products.

split_reasoning: Evaluating technology use and needs and recommending improvements form one assessment workflow.

parts.text: Evaluate organizational technology use and needs and recommend improvements.
parts.type_reasoning: The assessment produces recommendations that management can consider.
parts.unit_reasoning: A scoped assessment and its recommendations are handed over together.
parts.work_item: one technology needs assessment with recommendations
parts.start: technology area or organizational need is selected for assessment
parts.end: findings and recommended improvements are communicated to management
parts.checked_by: management and IT leadership
parts.overlap_reasoning: Consultations, strategic resource plans, and feasibility evaluations can share inputs or findings but have distinct purposes and outputs.

split_reasoning: Preparing or revising an operational budget and controlling individual expenditures are distinct activities.

parts.text: Prepare or revise the department's operational budget.
parts.type_reasoning: A budget is a distinct financial plan reviewed by management.
parts.unit_reasoning: The budget for a planning period is submitted and reviewed as a whole.
parts.work_item: one operational budget or budget revision
parts.start: budget period or need for revision is identified
parts.end: budget or revision is submitted for approval
parts.checked_by: finance and organizational management
parts.overlap_reasoning: Equipment purchases consume budget but are separate procurement actions.

parts.text: Review and control departmental expenditures against the operational budget.
parts.type_reasoning: An expenditure review produces a decision or disposition on a spending request.
parts.unit_reasoning: A spending request is reviewed and decided as an individual item.
parts.work_item: one expenditure request reviewed
parts.start: spending request or expenditure is presented for review
parts.end: approval, rejection, or follow-up is recorded or communicated
parts.checked_by: requesting staff and finance
parts.overlap_reasoning: An equipment purchase can include expenditure approval, but purchasing also includes procurement steps.

split_reasoning: Meetings with different parties share the same purpose of securing cooperation or resolving problems.

parts.text: Meet with managers, supervisors, vendors, and others to secure cooperation and resolve problems.
parts.type_reasoning: The target centers on live discussion and coordination rather than a specified document or decision artifact.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Some meetings may also assess computing needs, while each statement includes meetings for other purposes.

split_reasoning: Developing goals or policies and interpreting existing goals or policies are distinct activities; interpretation can occur live or in writing.

parts.text: Develop organizational goals, policies, or procedures.
parts.type_reasoning: A goal, policy, or procedure is a documented output for organizational use.
parts.unit_reasoning: A proposed or revised goal, policy, or procedure is submitted as a whole.
parts.work_item: one organizational goal, policy, or procedure drafted or revised
parts.start: need for a new or revised goal, policy, or procedure is identified
parts.end: draft is completed and submitted for approval
parts.checked_by: organizational management and affected staff
parts.overlap_reasoning: Departmental operating standards may also be organizational procedures, but both statements cover additional work.

parts.text: Interpret organizational goals, policies, or procedures for someone during a live contact.

parts.unit_reasoning: One interpretation request is answered within the live contact.
parts.work_item: one policy or procedure interpretation provided during a live contact
parts.start: person asks how a goal, policy, or procedure applies
parts.end: interpretation is explained to the person
parts.checked_by: the person requesting guidance
parts.overlap_reasoning: No other listed statement specifically covers this interpretation request.

parts.text: Respond to a written request to interpret organizational goals, policies, or procedures.
parts.type_reasoning: A written interpretation is a distinct response prepared outside a live contact.
parts.unit_reasoning: The response to one request is sent and relied on as a whole.
parts.work_item: one written policy or procedure interpretation
parts.start: written interpretation request is received
parts.end: written guidance is sent to the requester
parts.checked_by: the requester and, for sensitive cases, management
parts.overlap_reasoning: No other listed statement specifically covers this written interpretation.

notes: The relative amount of live and written interpretation depends on the organization.

split_reasoning: Recruiting and hiring, training, and supervising staff are different activities.

parts.text: Recruit candidates and participate in hiring decisions for computer-related staff.
parts.type_reasoning: Recruiting and selection for a vacancy produce a hiring recommendation or decision.
parts.unit_reasoning: The selection decision for a vacancy is the handoff to the hiring process.
parts.work_item: one staffing selection decision or recommendation
parts.start: vacancy and staffing requirements are identified
parts.end: candidate selection or hiring recommendation is communicated
parts.checked_by: human resources and the approving manager
parts.overlap_reasoning: No other listed statement specifically covers recruiting or hiring.

parts.text: Train computer-related staff.
parts.type_reasoning: The target describes instruction whose value lies in the live interaction with staff.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Training can occur during supervision, but the other statements do not specifically describe staff training.

parts.text: Supervise computer-related staff.
parts.type_reasoning: Supervision is primarily ongoing live direction and coaching of staff.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Supervision includes daily direction and may involve assigning or reviewing work, while those statements also specify their own outputs.

split_reasoning: Reviewing project plans to plan and coordinate activity is one planning workflow.

parts.text: Review project plans and plan and coordinate project activity.
parts.type_reasoning: The review produces a coordinated schedule or activity plan for project participants.
parts.unit_reasoning: The coordinated activity plan is the usable handoff to the project team.
parts.work_item: one coordinated project activity plan
parts.start: project plans are received for review
parts.end: activities, dependencies, and coordination arrangements are communicated to the project team
parts.checked_by: project team and project management
parts.overlap_reasoning: Project coordination can share priorities with daily departmental planning and draw on feasibility reviews, but those cover different outputs.

split_reasoning: Assessing feasibility and requirements are complementary parts of evaluating one proposal.

parts.text: Evaluate a data processing proposal for feasibility and requirements.
parts.type_reasoning: The evaluation produces a distinct assessment for a proposed project.
parts.unit_reasoning: A proposal is evaluated and its assessment communicated as a whole.
parts.work_item: one data processing proposal feasibility assessment
parts.start: proposal is submitted for evaluation
parts.end: feasibility findings and requirements are documented or communicated
parts.checked_by: project sponsor, management, and project team
parts.overlap_reasoning: Consultations and technology assessments can provide inputs, and project planning can follow the evaluation, but they are not identical work items.

split_reasoning: Preparing a report and reviewing someone else's report are different activities; operational and progress reports are alternative report subjects.

parts.text: Prepare an operational report or project progress report.
parts.type_reasoning: Each report is a distinct document sent to its readers.
parts.unit_reasoning: A report for a reporting period is prepared and submitted as a whole.
parts.work_item: one operational or project progress report prepared
parts.start: reporting period or request is established and source information is gathered
parts.end: completed report is submitted or distributed
parts.checked_by: management and report recipients
parts.overlap_reasoning: No other statement specifically covers preparing these reports.

parts.text: Review an operational report or project progress report prepared by someone else.
parts.type_reasoning: Each review produces feedback or approval on a submitted report.
parts.unit_reasoning: The submitted report is reviewed and returned or approved as a whole.
parts.work_item: one operational or project progress report reviewed
parts.start: report is received for review
parts.end: feedback or approval is returned to the preparer
parts.checked_by: report preparer and management
parts.overlap_reasoning: A report written by a direct report may also be a staff work product, but the broader staff review statement covers other outputs.

split_reasoning: Purchasing equipment is one procurement activity despite the different equipment or vendors involved.

split_reasoning: Technical support can be provided during live user contact, from a written queue afterward, or through hands-on work at equipment.

parts.text: Provide technical support while a user is on the phone, in chat, or present.
parts.type_reasoning: The user is waiting during troubleshooting and guidance.
parts.unit_reasoning: One reported problem is addressed within the live contact.
parts.work_item: one computer problem addressed during a live user contact
parts.start: user describes the computer problem during the contact
parts.end: guidance or the outcome is communicated to the user before the contact ends
parts.checked_by: the user and, where recorded, the support team
parts.overlap_reasoning: Some escalated help-service issues involve direct user support, while managing the help system also covers broader operations.

parts.text: Investigate and respond to a user's computer problem from a written request or support queue.
parts.type_reasoning: The support case is handled outside a live contact and produces a response or resolution.
parts.unit_reasoning: The queued support case is the unit tracked and handed back to the user.
parts.work_item: one queued computer support case addressed
